news.lead: Using the NASA/ESA/CSA James Webb Space Telescope, an international team of astronomers have discovered that dust and water can form and survive surprisingly close to the supermassive black hole at the centre of our Milky Way galaxy.

news.lead: Observing across the starry “plains” of space, the NASA/ESA/CSA James Webb Space Telescope has taken images of NGC 2392, nicknamed the Lion Nebula.

news.title: Webb Unravels Small Cosmic Details With Interferometry Observing Mode
news.lead: One of the most recognizable features of NASA’s James Webb Space Telescope is its large, segmented, gold-coated mirror, which delivers images twice as sharp as pre-launch estimates.

news.title: Photo Release: Webb uncovers unusual galaxy shaped by cosmic collision
news.lead: In new images from the NASA/ESA/CSA James Webb Space Telescope to celebrate its fourth science anniversary, a familiar galaxy transforms into something far richer, and far more complex, than ever seen before.

news.title: After Latest Swing Past Sun, NASA’s Parker Solar Probe Checks in
news.lead: NASA’s Parker Solar Probe completed its 29th close approach to the Sun on Sept. 4, again matching its record speed and distance from the solar surface.

news.title: Parker Solar Probe Makes 28th Close Pass of Sun
news.lead: NASA’s Parker Solar Probe completed its 28th close approach to the Sun on June 8, again matching its record distance of 3.8 million miles from the solar surface.

news.title: NASA’s Parker Solar Probe Makes 27th Swing Around the Sun
news.lead: NASA’s Parker Solar Probe completed its 27th close approach to the Sun on March 11, again matching its record distance of 3.8 million miles (6.2 million kilometers) from the solar surface.

news.title: NASA’s Parker Solar Probe Observes Interstellar Comet 3I/ATLAS
news.lead: NASA’s Parker Solar Probe observed interstellar comet 3I/ATLAS from Oct. 18 to Nov. 5, 2025, with its WISPR (Wide-Field Imager for Solar Probe) instrument.

news.title: NASA’s Parker Solar Probe Completes 26th Closest Approach to Sun
news.lead: NASA’s Parker Solar Probe completed its 26th close approach to the Sun on Dec. 13, again matching its record distance of 3.8 million miles (6.2 million kilometers) from the solar surface.

news.title: ESA’s Euclid captures the Milky Way’s crowded heart
news.lead: The largest and most detailed photo ever made of our Milky Way galaxy’s centre in visible light is revealed today by the European Space Agency’s Euclid mission.

news.title: Euclid Space Warps: help spot galaxies bending spacetime
news.lead: With the launch of Space Warps, a new citizen science project on the Zooniverse platform, you can now join in the search to find rare and elusive strong gravitational lenses in never-before-seen images captured by the European Space Agency’s Euclid space telescope.

news.title: Hubble & Euclid zoom into cosmic eye
news.lead: For this month’s ESA/Hubble Picture of the Month , NASA/ESA's Hubble Space Telescope is joined by ESA’s Euclid to create a new view of the most visually intricate remnants of a dying star: the Cat’s Eye Nebula, also known as NGC 6543.

news.title: NASA’s SPHEREx Observatory Maps Interstellar Ice in Milky Way
news.lead: An observation made by NASA’s SPHEREx (Spectro-Photometer for the History of the Universe, Epoch of Reionization, and Ices Explorer) shows the chemical signatures of water ice (shown in bright blue) and polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (orange) in Cygnus X, one of the most active and turbulent regions of star birth in our Milky Way galaxy.

news.title: NASA Space Telescope Maps Magnetic Fields of ‘Lighthouse’ Pulsar
news.lead: For the first time, scientists have used NASA’s IXPE (Imaging X-ray Polarimetry Explorer) to directly measure the magnetic fields of PSR J1101−6101, a pulsar located within what is often referred to as the Lighthouse Nebula.

news.title: NASA Engineers Help Prolong Voyager 2’s Science Mission
news.lead: Engineers at NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory have successfully freed up power on Voyager 2, extending how long the spacecraft can continue to do science.

news.title: NASA Shuts Off Instrument on Voyager 1 to Keep Spacecraft Operating
news.lead: On April 17, engineers at NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) in Southern California sent commands to shut down an instrument aboard Voyager 1 called the Low-energy Charged Particles experiment, or LECP.

news.title: Vintage NASA: See Voyager’s 1990 ‘Solar System Family Portrait’ Debut
news.lead: In archival footage of a historic NASA news conference, the mission reveals history-making images of six planets in our solar system, including a tiny speck called Earth.

news.title: NASA’s Voyager 1 Revives Backup Thrusters Before Command Pause
news.lead: The mission team wanted to fix the thrusters, deemed unusable decades ago, before the radio antenna that sends commands to the probe went offline for upgrades.

news.title: NASA Turns Off 2 Voyager Science Instruments to Extend Mission
news.lead: Mission engineers at NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory in Southern California turned off the cosmic ray subsystem experiment aboard Voyager 1 on Feb. 25 and will shut off Voyager 2’s low-energy charged particle instrument on March 24.
